topics.name: Readiness assessment
subtopics: Weeks 1-2 are allocated to readiness assessment alongside the number concept development activities listed for these weeks

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Counting
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 1 and 10 (weeks 1-4) and between 1 and 20 (weeks 5-10); describe the sequence
Link counting forwards to addition (one more) and counting backwards to subtraction (one less)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Mental maths (number range 5)
subtopics: Order a given set of numbers 1-5: first, last, in the middle
Compare numbers to 5 and say which is more or less; one more, one less, two more, two less (weeks 5-10)
Subitise: recognise how many objects are in a group without counting (dot cards)
What number comes after, before, between (weeks 5-10)
Techniques: put the larger number first to count on, number line, doubling and halving, building up and breaking down

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 10
subtopics: Give a reasonable estimate and check by counting out objects reliably; group counting

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols 1-20
Write number symbols and number names to 10

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order up to 5 objects
subtopics: Compare collections of objects: many, fewer, most, least (weeks 1-2); more than, less than (weeks 3-4, 9-10); the same as, just as many, different (weeks 5-8)
Order collections of objects from most to least and least to most

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 5 (number line)
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers: smaller than, greater than; more than, less than; is equal to; 1 more, 1 less; 2 more, 2 less
Order numbers smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest; before, after, between, in the middle; ascending and descending order on the number line 1-5
Identify, read and write number symbols and number names to 5; position 1st-5th on the number line (weeks 9-10)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context
subtopics: Practically solve problems in context and explain solutions involving addition and subtraction
Equal sharing and grouping problems that may include remainders
Techniques: concrete counters, drawings, number lines with concrete beads

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 5
subtopics: Addition and subtraction and number bonds up to 3 (weeks 1-4), up to 4 (weeks 5-6) and up to 5 (weeks 7-10)
Use the symbols +, -, = and □ in number sentences

topics.name: Measurement: Time
subtopics: Passing of time: compare lengths of time (longer, shorter, faster, slower); sequence events (yesterday, today, tomorrow)
Telling the time: describe when something happens (morning, afternoon, evening)
Name and sequence the days of the week and months of the year

topics.name: Measurement: Mass
subtopics: Estimate, measure, compare, order and record mass using non-standard measures
Vocabulary: heavy and light, more, less, big, small

topics.name: Space and shape: Position, orientation and views
subtopics: Describe the position of one object in relation to another: right, left, on top of, next to, in the middle, up, down

topics.name: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric and number patterns
subtopics: Copy and extend simple patterns using physical objects and drawings (colours and shapes)
Number patterns: copy, extend and describe number sequences in 1s to 50 forwards and backwards

topics.name: Space and shape: Position, orientation, views and direction
subtopics: Vocabulary: in front of, behind, left, right, next to, in the middle, up, down; vocabulary for comparing numbers
Follow directions to move around the classroom; follow simple instructions (put the ball next to the box)

topics.name: Data handling: Collect, sort and describe objects
subtopics: Collect, sort and describe objects (integrated with Numbers, operations and relationships)
Answer questions about the sorting process; draw a picture of sorted objects

topics.name: Remediation
subtopics: Supporting learning gaps: reteach using another strategy for improved learning; record findings where further support is required

topics.name: Consolidation
subtopics: Reinforce more of the same (practice) to embed knowledge and skills; give learners the opportunity to ask questions

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Repeat the knowledge and skills taught to establish whether learning has taken place, before new concepts are taught

sba: One formal assessment task (FAT) per term
Weeks 3-4: Space and shape (oral and practical); Patterns, functions and algebra (practical)
Weeks 5-6: Patterns, functions and algebra (written); Numbers, operations and relationships (oral, practical, written)
Weeks 7-8: Measurement (oral and practical); Data handling (written)

topics.name: Diagnostic assessment 1
subtopics: Weeks 1-2 are allocated to diagnostic assessment alongside the content listed for these weeks

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Counting
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 1 and 20 (weeks 1-2), 30 (weeks 3-4), 40 (weeks 5-6) and 50 (weeks 7-10)
Count forwards in 10s, 5s and 2s from any multiple of 10, 5 or 2 within the same ranges; see the relationship with addition (more than, ascending order)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Mental maths (number range 10)
subtopics: Order a given set of numbers: smallest to greatest, greatest to smallest; ascending and descending, left to right
Compare numbers to 5 (weeks 1-2), 7 (weeks 3-4), 9 (weeks 5-6) and 10 (weeks 7-10): which is more or less; recognise dot formations
Position: after, before, between, first, last, in the middle, left, right; use the number line

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 20
subtopics: Give a reasonable estimate and check by counting out objects reliably; group counting

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols 1-50
Write number symbols and number names to 10

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order up to 10 objects
subtopics: Compare collections of objects: many, fewer, most, least; more than, less than; the same as, just as many, different
Order collections of objects from most to least and least to most

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 10
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers: smaller than, greater than, is equal to; more than, less than; 1 more, 1 less; 2 more, 2 less
Order numbers: before, after, between, in the middle; ascending and descending on the number line 1-10
Identify, read and write numbers, symbols and number names; ordinal position 1st-10th on the number line (weeks 9-10)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context
subtopics: Solve problems in context and explain own solutions involving addition and subtraction, repeated addition (weeks 3-10), and equal sharing and grouping that may include remainders
Recognise South African currency; solve money problems involving totals and change
Techniques: concrete counters, drawings, building up and breaking down, doubling and halving, number lines with counting beads (CAPS pp. 45-46 problem types)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 10
subtopics: Addition and subtraction up to 6 (weeks 1-2), 7 (weeks 3-4), 8 (weeks 5-6), 9 (weeks 7-8) and 10 (weeks 9-10) using +, -, =, □
Practise number bonds up to 5 (weeks 1-2), 6 (weeks 3-4) and 7 (weeks 5-10)
Repeated addition using +, = and □

topics.name: Measurement: Time
subtopics: During whole class teaching: morning, afternoon, evening; a long time, a short time
Sequence the days of the week and months of the year; place birthdays on the calendar

topics.name: Measurement: Length
subtopics: Compare the length of objects; talk about comparisons: long, short, longer
Estimate and compare lengths: shorter, taller

topics.name: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric patterns
subtopics: Copy, extend and describe simple patterns; pack out objects (weeks 3-4)
Create and describe own patterns using physical objects; draw own simple patterns (weeks 7-8)

topics.name: Space and shape: 3D objects, position and 2D shapes
subtopics: 3D objects: position and directions; follow directions (right, left)
2D shapes: recognise and name circles, triangles and squares

topics.name: Data handling: Collect, sort and represent data
subtopics: Collect and sort objects; draw a picture of sorted objects; answer questions about the sorting process; describe sorted collections
Collect and organise data (e.g. a class birthday calendar); answer questions about data in a pictograph

topics.name: Remediation
subtopics: Supporting learning gaps: reteach using another strategy for improved learning; record findings where further support is required

topics.name: Consolidation
subtopics: Reinforce more of the same (practice) to embed knowledge and skills; give learners the opportunity to ask questions

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Repeat the knowledge and skills taught to establish whether learning has taken place, before new concepts are taught

sba: One formal assessment task (FAT) per term
Weeks 3-4: Data handling, Measurement, Patterns, functions and algebra (oral and practical)
Weeks 5-6: Numbers, operations and relationships; Patterns, functions and algebra (written)
Weeks 7-8: Space and shape; Data handling (written)
Weeks 9-10: Numbers, operations and relationships (oral and practical); Length (written)

topics.name: Diagnostic assessment 2
subtopics: Weeks 1-2 are allocated to diagnostic assessment alongside the content listed for these weeks

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Counting
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 1 and 50 (weeks 1-2), 60 (weeks 3-4), 70 (weeks 5-6) and 80 (weeks 7-10)
Count forwards in 10s, 5s and 2s from any multiple of 10, 5 or 2 within the same ranges; see the relationship with addition

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Mental maths (number range 15)
subtopics: Order a given set of numbers 1-10 (weeks 1-2), 1-12 (weeks 3-4) and 1-15 (weeks 5-10): smallest to greatest, ascending and descending
Compare numbers to 10, 12 and 15: more, less; after, before, between, first, last, left, right; use the number line
Rapid recall of number bonds; practise addition and subtraction facts to 5

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 40
subtopics: Give a reasonable estimate and check by counting out objects reliably; group counting

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols 1-80
Write number symbols and number names to 15

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order up to 15 objects
subtopics: Compare collections of objects: many, fewer, most, least; more than, less than; the same as, just as many, different
Order collections of objects from most to least and least to most

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 15
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers: smaller than, greater than; more than, less than; is equal to
Order numbers smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest; before, after, in the middle, between; use the number line 0-15

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value to 15
subtopics: Decompose 2-digit numbers into multiples of ten and ones (e.g. 11 is 10 and 1, 15 is 10 and 5)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context
subtopics: Solve problems in context and explain own solutions involving addition and subtraction, and equal sharing and grouping that may include remainders
Recognise South African currency; solve money problems involving totals and change

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 15
subtopics: Addition and subtraction up to 10 (weeks 1-4) and up to 15 (weeks 5-10) using +, -, =, □
Practise number bonds up to 7 (weeks 1-2), 8 (weeks 3-4) and 9 (weeks 5-10)
Repeated addition using +, = and □

topics.name: Space and shape: 3D objects and 2D shapes
subtopics: 3D objects: position and directions; follow directions (right, left)
2D shapes: recognise and name circles, triangles and squares

topics.name: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric patterns
subtopics: Copy, extend and describe simple patterns; pack out objects
Draw own simple patterns; create and describe own patterns

topics.name: Measurement: Time
subtopics: During whole class teaching: morning, afternoon, evening; days of the week; a long time, a short time
Sequence the days of the week and months of the year; place birthdays on the calendar

topics.name: Measurement: Capacity and volume
subtopics: Estimate, compare and order the amount of liquid that 2 containers can hold if filled
Language: more than, less than, full, empty; use non-standard measures (spoons, cups)

topics.name: Data handling: Collect, organise and represent data
subtopics: Integrated with Numbers, operations and relationships and Space and shape: collect and organise data about the school and learners' birthdays
Show data in a pictograph and answer questions about it

topics.name: Remediation
subtopics: Supporting learning gaps: reteach using another strategy for improved learning; record findings where further support is required

topics.name: Consolidation
subtopics: Reinforce more of the same (practice) to embed knowledge and skills; give learners the opportunity to ask questions

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Repeat the knowledge and skills taught to establish whether learning has taken place, before new concepts are taught

sba: One formal assessment task (FAT) per term
Weeks 3-4: Numbers, operations and relationships; Measurement (written); Data handling (oral)
Weeks 5-6: Numbers, operations and relationships; Patterns, functions and algebra; Space and shape (oral and practical)
Weeks 7-8: Numbers, operations and relationships; Patterns, functions and algebra; Space and shape (written)

topics.name: End-line assessment
subtopics: Weeks 1-2 are labelled end-line assessment alongside the content listed for these weeks

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Counting
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number between 1 and 80 (weeks 1-2), 90 (weeks 3-6) and 100 (weeks 7-10); link to one more, one less
Count forwards in 10s, 5s and 2s from any multiple of 10, 5 or 2 within the same ranges; see the relationship with addition

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Mental maths (number range 20)
subtopics: Order a given set of numbers 1-16 (weeks 1-2), 1-17 (weeks 3-4), 1-18 (weeks 5-6), 1-20 (weeks 7-8): ascending and descending, left to right
Compare numbers to 16, 17, 18 and 15: more, less; after, before, between, first, last, left, right; use the number line
Rapid recall of number bonds and addition and subtraction facts to 8 (weeks 1-4), 9 (weeks 5-6) and 10 (weeks 7-10)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Count objects reliably to 50
subtopics: Give a reasonable estimate and check by counting out objects; group counting

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Number symbols and number names
subtopics: Recognise, identify and read number symbols 1-100
Write number symbols and number names to 20

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order up to 20 objects
subtopics: Compare collections of objects: many, fewer, most, least; more than, less than; the same as, just as many, different
Order collections of objects from most to least and least to most

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Describe, compare and order numbers to 20
subtopics: Describe and compare numbers: smaller than, greater than, more than, less than, is equal to
Order numbers smallest to greatest and greatest to smallest; before, after, in the middle, between; use the number line 0-20
Use ordinal numbers to show order, place and position: first, second, third ... tenth, last

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value to 20
subtopics: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of ten and ones (e.g. 16 is 10 and 6; 19 is 1 ten and 9 ones; 20 is 2 tens and 0 ones)

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context (at least 20)
subtopics: Solve problems in context and explain own solutions involving addition and subtraction, and equal sharing and grouping that may include remainders
Recognise South African currency; solve money problems involving totals and change

topics.name: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 20
subtopics: Addition and subtraction up to 16 using +, -, =, □
Practise number bonds up to 8
Repeated addition using +, = and □

topics.name: Measurement: Time
subtopics: During whole class teaching: morning, afternoon, evening; days of the week; a long time, a short time
Sequence the days of the week and months of the year; place birthdays on the calendar

topics.name: Data handling: Collect, sort and represent objects
subtopics: Collect and sort objects, discuss sorted collections and represent sorted objects

topics.name: Patterns, functions and algebra: Geometric patterns
subtopics: Copy, extend and describe simple patterns; pack out objects
Draw own simple patterns; create and describe own pattern
Number patterns are integrated with counting

topics.name: Consolidation

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Repeat the knowledge and skills taught to establish whether learning has taken place, before new concepts are taught

Weeks 3-4: Numbers, operations and relationships; Data handling (written and practical)
Weeks 5-6: Numbers, operations and relationships; Measurement; Space and shape (written)
Weeks 7-10: Numbers, operations and relationships; Patterns, functions and algebra; Space and shape (oral and written)
